architecture_recovery.honesty: ENVELOPE-FORCED: epoxy-polyamide, 1:1 volume, solvent-borne, VOC<=340. INDEPENDENTLY RECOVERED by the zero-prior funnel and CONFIRMED against the government F160/F161 slash sheets on the 8 COMPUTED checks above (epoxy EEW in the 175-195 gov band = 188.5, reactive-polyamide curative, silicate-class extender = ['silica'], gov-precedent solvent families, sub-stoichiometric R matching gov F160's own R~0.78). The two pot-life/color items are DESIGN CHOICES consistent with the class, reported separately and NOT counted as recovery. DIVERGENCES (honest): the government uses SiO2 silica as the bulk extender loaded mainly on the epoxy side; the engine may use other silicate-class minerals split across both components; which side is labelled 'A' vs 'B' is inverted (chemically identical two-component epoxy/polyamide split).

f160_pvc_benchmark.honesty: The Navy's OWN qualified black primer (Formula 160) is RESIN-RICH: PVC ~8% (barrier by crosslink density + a modest silica extender, NOT by heavy filler). The 32-38% PVC figure is the FILLED anticorrosive-SPF style (Evonik commercial guides) -- a different, equally valid barrier philosophy. The engine lead sits BETWEEN, closer to the government primer. There are two legitimate barrier strategies; the blueprint follows the government's.
